facts.text: Virtual Seduction was part of Roger Corman Presents, a Showtime series. Showtime came to Corman with the idea, then picked remakes for season one using market research.
Showtime's Roger Corman Presents squeezed in sci-fi and horror shoots across Los Angeles, plus one movie shot in Moscow and another in Manila, says Corman.
Roger Corman Presents shot 13 films by mid-June 1995 at roughly $1.5 million each. Corman said: "I don't think a day went by that we weren't shooting."
Virtual Seduction was the fourth episode of Roger Corman Presents' first season. Nine of that season's films were originals, and one, Terminal Virus, was a bought-in script.
Ami Dolenz (Laura) refused a nude scene. A producer asked why she took an erotic thriller if she wouldn't get naked. She has always opposed on-screen nudity.
Jeff Fahey's earlier VR film The Lawnmower Man (1992) led Stephen King to sue to remove his name from it. It used only his title and a few elements, and began life as a script called Cyber God.
Carrie Genzel, who plays Paris, did her first nude scene in this film. She later turned up in The Walking Dead, Supernatural and Watchmen.
The Lawnmower Man's effects came from Angel Studios, later Rockstar San Diego. Den of Geek says it likely has the first CG love scene in film. Virtual Seduction's VR is far humbler.
Ami Dolenz is the daughter of Monkees drummer Micky Dolenz and Samantha Juste, a 1960s TV pop-show hostess. Her childhood neighbor was Alice Cooper.
The script is credited to Michelle Gamble-Risley, William Widmaier and director Paul Ziller. Gamble-Risley and Widmaier also get the story credit.
Star Jeff Fahey played the VR-obsessed Jobe in The Lawnmower Man (1993). Two years later he was back in cyberspace for Corman's Showtime series.
Producer Mike Elliott made this for New Horizons, Roger Corman's low-budget outfit. Richard Scheib's Moria review credits the production to that company.
Before acting, Jeff Fahey won a full scholarship to the Joffrey Ballet School at age 25. He studied there for three years and also taught ballroom dancing.
Meshach Taylor (Anderson) was an Emmy nominee for Designing Women. He also played window dresser Hollywood Montrose in Mannequin (1987) and its 1991 sequel.
Director Paul Ziller says working for Roger Corman taught him to make films on tight budgets. The Directors Guild of Canada says producers praise his 'much higher quality film than expected'.
Director Paul Ziller is an NYU Film School grad who started out writing, directing and editing for Roger Corman. He later spent nearly a decade making Syfy movies.
Director Paul Ziller also made Swarmed, Stonehenge Apocalypse and the Syfy film The Philadelphia Experiment (2012), according to Richard Scheib's Moria review.
Moria's Richard Scheib gave the film 2 stars. He said it's not really erotica despite the title, with only one erotic scene, and called the VR sequences 'ordinary rooms and restaurants'.
Corman's Showtime series had one reject. The Haunted Sea (1997) was meant as an episode, but Showtime said it didn't meet its quality standards, so it premiered on home video.
Virtual Seduction was shot in Vancouver. Director Paul Ziller later settled there and went on to direct Hallmark romantic comedies.
The film rode the 1990s virtual-reality wave of Brainscan, Virtuosity and The Lawnmower Man, years before The Matrix (1999), says Richard Scheib's Moria review.
Ami Dolenz's archive footage was used for the CD-ROM game Bloodwings: Pumpkinhead's Revenge (1995). She didn't know until it was in stores.
Ami Dolenz is friends with 'Weird Al' Yankovic. He pretended to saw her in half onstage during 'Like a Surgeon'.
Jeff Fahey later played pilot Frank Lapidus on Lost (2008-2010). He also teamed with director Robert Rodriguez on Planet Terror, Machete and Alita: Battle Angel.
The Roger Corman Presents series ran 30 films over two seasons, including Black Scorpion, Piranha and Vampirella. Virtual Seduction first aired on Showtime on August 1, 1995.
Jeff Fahey's Psycho III (1986) role as Duane Duke came nine years before this. Wikipedia lists the Clint Eastwood film White Hunter Black Heart among his notable roles.
Meshach Taylor died in 2014 at age 67. He was best known as Anthony Bouvier on Designing Women (1986-93).
